title: Prime-power Gysin classes on regular schemes and their localizations
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and let $u:U\to V$ be a separated compactifiable finite-type morphism between regular affine Noetherian excellent schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use ordinary etale exceptional pullback [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] and signed roots-of-unity twists [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. Locally $u$ factors as a regular closed immersion followed by a smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Here a regular closed immersion has ideal locally generated by a finite sequence each of whose elements is a nonzerodivisor modulo its predecessors. Its codimension is the length of this sequence. The virtual relative dimension $e$ is the smooth relative dimension minus that codimension. If $V=\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $U$ is integral, $e=\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(\eta_U)$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree, def-weil-residue-field]. There is an isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Cl}_u:\Lambda_U(e)[2e]\xrightarrow{\sim}u^!\Lambda_V.$$
For a regular closed immersion it is the absolute-purity fundamental class: locally it is the product of the codimension-one Kummer boundary classes of a defining regular sequence. For a smooth morphism it is the diagonal/deformation orientation of [lem-trf-ambient-diagonal-purity-base-change]. For a factorization it is the composite of these two classes. It is independent of the factorization and of the regular sequence, commutes with etale localization, source and target open restriction, and regular change of base. For composable such regular morphisms $U\xrightarrow uV\xrightarrow vW$, under exceptional transitivity and the canonical twist identifications,
$$\operatorname{Cl}_{vu}=u^!(\operatorname{Cl}_v)\circ\operatorname{Cl}_u(e_v)[2e_v].$$
The same statements hold for essentially finite-type morphisms obtained by localizing these regular schemes, using the model restrictions of [lem-per-prime-power-supported-calculus]; in particular they apply to finitely generated towers of fields. For a finite purely inseparable extension $L/K$ in characteristic $p\ne\ell$, the class of $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is multiplication by $[L:K]$ under the tautological etale equivalence $a^!\Lambda_K\cong\Lambda_L$. Thus it is a unit, but it is not in general the identity.

source.place: XVI, Definition 2.1.1, Theorem 2.3.2, Theorems 2.5.5 and 2.5.12, Theorem 3.1.1 and Corollary 3.1.2; XVII, Proposition 2.4.3.3 proof and Lemmas 2.4.3.4, 4.3.1.2. Smooth orientation is specified by the current blueprint diagonal/deformation route

proof.text:
Work componentwise when the virtual dimension varies. By [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus], an affine finite-type presentation embeds $U$ regularly in $\mathbf A^r_V$, and every smooth/regular factorization gives the same locally constant integer $e=r-c$. This proves the asserted local factorization and independence of its dimension. The same node gives
$$e=\dim\mathcal O_{U,y}-\dim\mathcal O_{V,u(y)}+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(u(y))}\kappa(y).$$
For $V=\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $y=\eta_U$, both local rings in this formula are fields, of dimension zero; hence $e=\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(\eta_U)$.

source.place: XVI Definitions 2.5.1–2.5.3; affine regular factorization and intrinsic dimension formula

proof.text: For a regular closed immersion $i$ of codimension $c$, take the supported class $\eta_i:\Lambda\to i^!\Lambda(c)[2c]$ of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus], or equivalently its twist $\operatorname{Cl}_i:\Lambda(-c)[-2c]\to i^!\Lambda$. On a regular-sequence chart $Z_k=V(t_1,\ldots,t_k)$, that node states exactly that $\eta_i$ is the composite of the adjoints of the Cartier Kummer maps $c_{Z_k,\Lambda}$ of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer]. Thus the local product in the statement uses the supported Chern/Kummer normalization $+c_1(\mathcal O(Z_k))$, not an unspecified sign for a localization connecting map. The intermediate $Z_k$ need not be regular: both cited class statements allow arbitrary Noetherian Cartier pairs. Independence of generators and their order is part of the class-calculus statement. For the original regular pair, [lem-per-gabber-regular-pair-purity] makes this map an isomorphism.

For the smooth factor $p$, use the isomorphism $\gamma_p:\Lambda(r)[2r]\to p^!\Lambda$ of [lem-per-noetherian-prime-power-smooth-duality]. Its inverse is diagonal restriction, deformation to the zero section of $T_{P/V}$, and inverse Kummer-normalized vector-bundle purity. These are precisely the three maps defining the inverse orientation in [lem-trf-ambient-diagonal-purity-base-change] at $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$; therefore the smooth orientation has the normalization required by the item. Both statements concern ordinary etale adjoints; their common adjoint is identified by uniqueness of a right adjoint. No trace-based smooth-purity construction is used.

source.place: Current blueprint smooth-purity orientation: diagonal, deformation and vector-bundle normalization; finite coefficient specialization

proof.text:
For $u=pi$ form $a_{p,i}:=i^!(\gamma_p)\circ\operatorname{Cl}_i(r)[2r]$ using exceptional transitivity. Its source is $\Lambda(r-c)[2(r-c)]$, and it is an isomorphism since its two factors are. The statement of [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity] calls its Gysin isomorphism canonical but does not display its constituents. By that node's construction (its proof, step 3; a definitional unfolding, not a further theorem) its class for $f=pi$ is $a_p\star a_i$, with $a_i$ the supported Kummer class of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] used in step 2 and $a_p$ the shifted diagonal/DNC orientation of [lem-per-noetherian-prime-power-smooth-duality] used in step 3. Undoing the twist normalization, this is $a_{p,i}$; so $a_{p,i}$ is the class $\operatorname{Cl}_{u,n}$ of that node, and its assertions apply to it. They give independence of the factorization, the identity normalization, and
$$\operatorname{Cl}_{vu}=u^!(\operatorname{Cl}_v)\circ\operatorname{Cl}_u(e_v)[2e_v].$$
Here $e_{vu}=e_u+u^*e_v$, and the twist identifications are those in the stated exceptional-transitivity assertion. The same node gives etale localization and target open restriction (an etale base change). For a source open immersion $j:U'\hookrightarrow U$, factor $j$ as the codimension-zero identity immersion followed by the relative-dimension-zero smooth map $j$; by [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus, lem-per-noetherian-prime-power-smooth-duality] both classes are the identity and the etale adjunction comparison $\Lambda_{U'}\cong j^!\Lambda_U=j^*\Lambda_U$, so the composition formula gives $\operatorname{Cl}_{uj}=j^*\operatorname{Cl}_u$.

source.place: XVI Definition 2.5.11, Theorems 2.5.5 and 2.5.12, Corollary 3.1.2; smooth classes interpreted with step 3

proof.text: For regular base change $h:V'\to V$, pull back the chosen factorization $U\hookrightarrow P\to V$. By [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus], flat base change preserves the regular closed immersion and its codimension. The supported class of the closed immersion commutes with this flat base change by [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus]. The smooth factor and its orientation commute with this base change by [lem-per-noetherian-prime-power-smooth-duality]. The supported exchange is compatible with exceptional transitivity and counit-defined tensor maps by [lem-per-prime-power-supported-calculus]. Thus pulling back the composite of step 4 gives the composite for the pulled-back factorization, hence its canonical class by factorization independence. This proves regular-base-change compatibility, including the specified exceptional comparison.

source.place: XVI Proposition 2.2.3.1; XVII Lemma 4.3.1.2; supported exchange and smooth base-change compatibility

proof.text: For an essentially finite-type map, restrict a finite-type model and its class. The exceptional target and composition comparisons are independent of the model by [lem-per-prime-power-supported-calculus]. Localization of the base uses the localization assertion of [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity]. For a finitely generated field extension $L=K(x_1,\ldots,x_m)$ take $A=K[x_1,\ldots,x_m]\subset L$. The field $K$ is excellent [lem-exc-fields-excellent], so every localization of a finite-type $K$-algebra is excellent [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]; by J-2 [def-exc-excellent-ring] the regular locus of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is open, and it contains the generic point, whose local ring is the field $L$. A basic open $\operatorname{Spec}A[1/g]$ inside it is a regular affine Noetherian excellent model. Two such models $A_1,A_2\subset L$ have a common basic open: $A_{12}=A_1[A_2]\subset L$ is generated over $A_1$ by finitely many fractions, so $A_{12}\subset A_1[1/g_1]$ and $A_1[1/g_1]=A_{12}[1/g_1]$, likewise for $A_2$; then $A_{12}[1/g_1g_2]$ is a basic open of both, compatibly with $L$. By the source-open-restriction clause of step 4 the two classes restrict to the class of this common model, hence agree on $\operatorname{Spec}L$. For a tower $K\subset M\subset L$ with $L=M(y_1,\ldots,y_k)$ and $M$-model $\operatorname{Spec}A_M$, take $A_M[y_1,\ldots,y_k]\subset L$, shrunk to a regular basic open as above, as a model of $L/M$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A_M$. The composition and normalization equalities of steps 4-5 hold on these finite-type models and restrict to $\operatorname{Spec}L$ by the pseudofunctor and composition clause of [lem-per-prime-power-supported-calculus].

source.place: XVII Proposition 2.4.3.1 and Lemma 4.4.1 proofs, using model-independent localized exceptional restriction

proof.text: It remains to compute the purely inseparable scalar rather than introduce it as another lemma. By [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-pth-root-tower], a finite purely inseparable extension in characteristic $p$ is a tower of degree-$p$ extensions $K_j=K_{j-1}(\alpha_j)$ with $\alpha_j^p=b_j\in K_{j-1}$. First fix one such extension $L=K(\alpha)$, $[L:K]=p$. Factor $a:\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ as the Cartier immersion $i:V(t^p-b)\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_K$ followed by its smooth projection $q$. Both factors are between regular schemes; their virtual dimensions are $-1$ and $1$, so $e_a=0$.

source.place: XVII Proposition 2.4.3.3 proof (finite radicial scalar); fields.tex Tag 09HI, lemma-finite-purely-inseparable

proof.text: The morphism $a$ is a universal homeomorphism: [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep] says that its base change to every $K$-scheme is a homeomorphism. By [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance], $a^*$ and $a_*$ are inverse exact equivalences, also on complexes. Choose the proper compactification $(1,a)$. The formula $Ra_!=Ra_*D1_!$ in [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and exactness of the equivalence $a_*$ give $Ra_!=a_*$. Its right adjoint $a^!$ is consequently $a^*$ by uniqueness of right adjoints. The class of $a$ is therefore multiplication by a scalar $\lambda\in\Lambda$. To compute it one may equivalently compute its adjoint $\tau_a:a_*\Lambda_L\to\Lambda_K$ and then apply the faithful equivalence $a^*$; the unit and counit of the equivalence identify both source and target with the constant line.

source.place: XVII Proposition 2.4.3.3 proof, tautological etale identifications for finite radicial fields

proof.text: Let $G_i:Ri_*\Lambda_L\to\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_K}(1)[2]$ be the supported Cartier map of step 2. By the adjunction formula for the composite in step 4, its pushforward followed by the smooth counit is $\tau_a$. Base change from $K$ to $L$ takes this formula to $Rq_{L,!}(G_{i'})$ followed by the smooth counit over $L$: compact-support exchange is compatible with composition by [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], and the smooth orientation and its adjoint trace commute with base change by [lem-trf-ambient-diagonal-purity-base-change]. Flat base change of the supported immersion class is [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus]. Here $i':D=V((t-\alpha)^p)\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_L$. Its source is nonreduced, which is allowed in that class-calculus statement; no absolute-purity theorem is applied to $D$.

source.place: XVI Proposition 2.2.3.1; current diagonal/DNC smooth base change; ordinary compact-support exchange

proof.text: Put $s=V(t-\alpha)$. The inclusion $s\hookrightarrow D$ is a universal homeomorphism: after every base change the nilpotent ideal $(t-\alpha)$ remains nilpotent and is contained in every prime, so it does not change the prime spectrum or its closed subsets. Topological invariance [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance] identifies the constant sheaves on $D$ and $s$ and their closed pushforwards. In the supported Cartier construction of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer], the pair $(\mathcal O(p s),1)$ is the $p$-fold tensor power of $(\mathcal O(s),1)$. In a local trivialization its invertible function off $s$ is $(t-\alpha)^p$. The Kummer connecting homomorphism sends this to $p\kappa(t-\alpha)$, and the supported boundary is additive as well. Therefore $G_{i'}=pG_s$ under the identified supported sources. This is just additivity of the defining connecting homomorphisms, with the same sign on both sides.

source.place: XVI section 2.1 (supported Kummer class of a pseudo-divisor); elementary tensor-power calculation

proof.text: The point $s$ is a closed section of $q_L:\mathbf A^1_L\to\operatorname{Spec}L$. The section identity of [lem-per-smooth-gysin-mixed-identities] says that the supported class of $s$, integrated using the same smooth orientation, is $1_\Lambda$. Step 10 thus makes the base-changed adjoint class $\tau_a$ equal to $p\,1_\Lambda$. Faithfulness in step 8 gives $\lambda=p$ over $K$, proving the degree-$p$ scalar without using exceptional base change for a nonregular field extension. Only compact-support base change and flat base change of the supported class were used.

source.place: XVI section 2.1 and section identity of Lemma 2.5.8, with diagonal/DNC normalization; XVII Proposition 2.4.3.3 scalar calculation

proof.text: Now induct along the tower of step 7. The empty tower is the identity class. Each further degree-$p$ step contributes scalar $p$ by steps 8–11, and the composition formula of step 4 multiplies these scalars. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] their product is $[L:K]=p^r$. Since $p\ne\ell$, Bezout gives an inverse of $p^r$ modulo $\ell^n$, so the scalar is a unit. It need not be $1$: for $K=\mathbf F_2(z)$, $L=K(z^{1/2})$, $\ell=3$, $n=1$, the scalar is $2\ne1$. This completes the last clause and all clauses of the item.

source.place: XVII Proposition 2.4.3.3 proof; finite-tower degree formula and elementary coefficient arithmetic

A regular base change is flat; lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus states that flat base change keeps a regular closed immersion and its codimension; lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus states that its class commutes with flat base change of pairs; smooth-duality gives Noetherian base change of the orientation; supported-calculus gives the regular supported exchange compatible with transitivity.
